title: Signal-led onboarding: affinity fingerprints & auto-release briefs
author: Maya Thompson
ci_status: fail -> pass (initial lint/format error fixed in follow-up commit)
description: Motivation: onboarding teams currently hand-author model release notes and pick variant names independently from runtime signal characteristics. This PR introduces a lightweight signal-led onboarding flow that (1) fingerprints hardware affinity and runtime performance from sampled production traces, (2) generates a canonical alias map for model variants tied to provenance and quantization knobs, and (3) seeds concise, telemetry-driven release briefs (auto-briefs) that summarize expected throughput/latency/quality tradeoffs. Design summary: the feature adds a sampling shim in the runtime ingestion path that emits anonymized micro-traces to the registry CLI; a new registry service component (affinity fingerprint store) computes compact affinity signatures and associates them with model uploads; a variant-canonicalizer layer resolves incoming variant aliases into stable canonical IDs and records provenance metadata for rollbacks; finally an autobrief generator produces a short structured paragraph and a one-line changelog entry using sampled percentile metrics and a templated blurb engine. This PR implements the end-to-end pipeline, a CLI hook (redwood-registry onboard --seed-sample), a lightweight validation step for alias collisions, and a UI metadata field for the Console to display the generated brief. Checklist: [x] sampling shim + telemetry contract defined [x] affinity fingerprint compute + persistence implemented [x] alias canonicalizer + collision tests implemented [x] autobrief generator with templated summaries [x] CLI hook and CI e2e smoke [x] unit tests and linters passing after fix. Backwards compatibility: variant aliasing is opt-in for existing onboarding flows via a flag; canonical IDs are additive and do not change prior model IDs. Security/PII: sampling emits only aggregate timing/shape metrics and truncated cache-key hashes; no user prompt text leaves the registry. Rollout plan: 1) enable sampling at 1% for internal canaries, 2) run offline reconciliation for 48 hours, 3) turn on autobrief drafts in Console as reviewable until a model owner approves, 4) enable automated brief publishing for models on the digital-signing allowlist. Related Linear: ENG-1462 (onboard telemetry contract), PM-921 (autobrief UX rubric). Why different: unlike previous changelog automation, this ties release notes to observed runtime signal distributions and hardware affinity so engineers get a preview of how variants behave in target fleets. Known limitations: affinity fingerprint convergence may need >100 samples for tail percentiles; autobrief phrasing is intentionally conservative and includes an explicit confidence band.
